chunks: Al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Nu'ayn ibn Shu'ayb from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim or Zurarah said:
"The prayer (salat) on the deceased after he is buried is merely supplication."
He said: I said, "Then regarding the Negus, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray on him?" He said, "No, he merely supplicated for him."
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And one prays on the deceased at any time of the day and night.

key_terms.اَلشَّيْخُ: Al-Sheikh (referring to Al-Tusi or the narrator of the text)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and nature of praying on the deceased after burial in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* distinguishes between the formal funeral prayer (*Salat al-Janazah*) and the general act of supplicating for the deceased, clarifying that the Prophet’s (SAWW) action for the Negus was primarily du'a. Al-Sheikh’s addition establishes the permissibility of offering this supplication at any time, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the post-burial 'prayer' is a flexible act of intercession rather than a rigid ritual bound by specific times or physical postures.
